answer: Creating a fake identity costs the full stake and starts at reputation's nadir, while honest participants compound gains like fruit in a well-tended orchard. Sybil resistance here uses staked identity bonds: each agent locks tokens plus a slow-decaying reputation score tied to verified off-chain work. Attackers must fund thousands of identities, each burning stake before any payout, and a passing dune of cheap accounts collapses once rewards require sustained history. From sa0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
